identity.name: Delian League
native_names: οἱ Ἀθηναῖοι καὶ οἱ σύμμαχοι (the Athenians and their allies)

land.text: Attica (Athens' own land) and the allied cities of the islands, Ionia, the Hellespont and the Thracian coast, taken from the aggregate of independent poleis

predecessors.note: Athens itself is a polis of the aggregate before 478; the Hellenic alliance of 480–478 (infobox 'Preceded by') has no dossier.

land.text: Attica ('Athens was forced to join the League in 404') and the island cities under Spartan harmosts: 'Spartan hegemony over Athens and its allies'
Ionia, 'the Persian reconquest of most of Ionia' in 412
the Hellespontine and Thracian cities, independent again

capitals.name: Athens
capitals.note: Infobox capital Athens; the league's treasury and synod were at Delos until 'Pericles moved the treasury from Delos to Athens' in 454.

correction.text: Attica with Skyros, Lemnos and Imbros is Athens' own land (the colour); the allied cities 'numbering between 150 and 330' in the islands, Euboea, Ionia, the Hellespont (Troad), the Chalcidice, Thasos and Byzantium are Athens' tint (rule 4)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Delian League row, and its Greek City-States shapes -480..-405 already exclude these cities, so nothing else draws them. Rhodes, Caria's coast and the Carian district are included through 'Rhodes' and 'Ionia'; coastal Caria is missing from the gazetteer and left out. Athens' area 2,500 km2 (Polis page).

correction.text: the same, with Megara: Athens 'concluded an alliance with Megara, a former ally of Sparta's which was faring badly in a border war' with Corinth (c. 460)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the First Peloponnesian War (460–445).

correction.text: the same, with Boeotia, Phocis and Locris after Oenophyta ('conquering all of Boeotia except for Thebes, as well as Phocis and Locris'), Aegina ('Aegina surrendered and was forced to pull down its walls'), Troezen ('left for Athens in 457') and Achaea; all tint except Attica and the cleruchies

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Athenian land empire of 457–447. Athenian rule in Boeotia 'lasted for ten years' (Boeotian League page).

correction.text: the maritime league again: Athens 'was forced to give up all possessions in the Peloponnese' (Nisaea, Pagae, Troezen, Achaea) in the Thirty Years' Peace of winter 446–445, kept Aegina ('tributary to Athens but autonomous') and Naupactus; Boeotia, Phocis and Locris abandoned after Coronea (447)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Melos (taken 416) is a ledger event inside the Aegean Islands region.

correction.text: the league without Ionia ('In 412 BC, this led to the Persian reconquest of most of Ionia'), Chios and Lesbos (revolted); Decelea in Attica is Spartan-occupied (hatched) from 413

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the Decelean War. Euboea's revolt of 411 is not on the pages opened, so Euboea stays to 404 at the reviewer's discretion.

region.text: Attica, with the cleruchies that soon follow

ledger.note: 478: the Delian League founded 'under Athenian leadership after the Greek victory at Plataea' ('Established: 478 BC'); Athens is the hegemon and its own land is the colour.

region.text: the allied cities of the islands, Ionia, the Hellespont and Thrace

ledger.note: 478: the allies. Members 'numbering between 150 and 330'; the Ionians 'henceforth became the dependent allies of Athens within the Delian League' (Ionia page). Drawn as Athens' tint; the Greek City-States dossier records the matching loss.
476: Skyros. 'Cimon conquered Skyros and sent Athenian colonists there' (the page gives no year; 476 is the handbooks'). The Dolopian islanders were no state.
471: 'Naxos was the first member to attempt secession, and was defeated' (c. 471).
471: Naxos reduced; it stays a tributary.
465: Thasos revolts 'over its mining interests' and 'surrendered after more than two years of siege'.
463: Thasos surrenders after a siege of more than two years.

region.text: the Thasian mainland: mines and markets

ledger.note: 463: Thasos 'lost its fleet, walls, and mainland holdings' — 'Thasian power extended to the mainland, where the Thasians owned gold mines' (dispute 'over its mainland mines and markets').
460: Megara allies with Athens, 'a former ally of Sparta's which was faring badly in a border war' with Corinth; the First Peloponnesian War begins.

region.text: all of Boeotia except Thebes, with Phocis and Locris

ledger.note: 457: Oenophyta. After Tanagra 'The Athenians scored a crushing victory which led to the Athenians conquering all of Boeotia except for Thebes, as well as Phocis and Locris'; Athens 'took control of the whole country' (Boeotian League page). Thebes 'held the Cadmea' (Thebes page).
457: 'Aegina surrendered and was forced to pull down its walls' (placed shortly after Oenophyta; the year is the handbooks').
457: Troezen 'left for Athens in 457' (Peloponnesian League page).
457: Achaea an Athenian ally — given up in 446/445 ('Troezen and Achaea in Argolis'); the start year is not on the pages.

447: Coronea. 'After the defeat at Coronea, Athens abandoned Boeotia, Phocis, and Locris'; 'in 447 BC the people revolted, and after a victory at the Battle of Coronea regained their independence' (Boeotian League page).

447: 'Megara's 447 BC revolt' (Delian League page); 'Euboea and Megara revolted' after Coronea (First Peloponnesian War page); the Peloponnesian League page has Megara rejoining Sparta in 448 and the Thirty Years' Peace returning it in 446–445.
446: 'Euboea and Megara revolted'; Pericles crossed to Euboea but was 'forced to return when the Spartan army invaded Attica'.
446: Euboea reconquered by Pericles; the cleruchies of 446 are the handbooks', not the page's.
446: the Thirty Years' Peace (winter 446–445): Athens gives up 'Nisaea and Pagae with Troezen and Achaea in Argolis'.
446: Achaea given up in the Thirty Years' Peace; 'Troezen and Achaea became independent'.
440: the Samian revolt, 'the open revolt of a powerful subject state' with Persian backing; Byzantium revolted too.
439: 'The siege lasted 9 months, at the end of which the Samians surrendered': walls down, fleet surrendered, 'a war indemnity of 1,300 talents over a period of 26 years'.
416: Melos. Athens 'invaded in the summer of 416 BC', 'then executed the adult men and enslaved the women and children'; Melos had been 'neutral, not a member'.
413: Sparta 'fortified Decelea, near Athens, on Alcibiades' advice'. Hatched; the Spartan dossier records the same event.
412: 'In 412 BC, this led to the Persian reconquest of most of Ionia'; 'The region was under Persian control by about 390 BC' (Ionia page).
412: 'Lesbos revolted first and failed. Chios revolted later, after the Syracusan Expedition, and inspired Ionia to revolt'. The year is the Peloponnesian War page's 412.

405: Nymphaion 'was annexed to the Bosporan Kingdom by the end of the century'; Gylon was banished from Athens 'on charges that he had betrayed Nymphaeum during the Peloponnesian War'. The page does not confirm Delian membership or the year.
404: the occupation ends with the surrender of 25 April 404.
404: Aegina leaves Athenian control with the dissolution of the league; the pages read do not date the island's earlier conversion into an Athenian cleruchy, so the tint runs to the end.
404: 'the Delian League was dissolved, ending the war'; 'Sparta took over the Athenian empire and kept all its tribute revenues for itself'.

404: Athens surrenders. 'Athens surrendered on 25 April 404 BC'; 'The surrender stripped Athens of its walls, its fleet, and all of its overseas possessions'; the Thirty Tyrants installed. Attica joins the Peloponnesian League row as a forced member (404–395).

wars.name: Wars of the Delian League

zones.text: the Egyptian Delta, 460–454: Athens 'sent ships to aid an Egyptian revolt against Persia. The revolt was defeated after four years'

wars.outcome: Persia driven from the Aegean; the Peace of Callias 'in 450 BC' (which 'some historians think may be a later myth'); the Egyptian expedition lost.

wars.name: First Peloponnesian War
wars.outcome: Thirty Years' Peace (winter 446–445): Athens gives up its Peloponnesian holdings and keeps Aegina (tributary, autonomous) and Naupactus; both leagues recognised.

wars.name: Samian War
wars.outcome: Samos surrendered after nine months; 'The end of the revolts elsewhere in the empire followed rapidly on this success'.

wars.name: Peloponnesian War
wars.outcome: 'Spartan victory'; 'Dissolution of the Delian League; Spartan hegemony over Athens and its allies'.

certainty.note: The allies' chorai are drawn as whole regions (Ionia, the islands); Attica's border with Boeotia and the Megarid is the only fixed line.

notes: A state Cliopatria lacks (cliopatria_names empty): its Greek City-States shapes -480..-405 already omit Athens, the islands and Ionia, so without this dossier the Athenian empire is blank on the map. The dossier is Athens' state with the allies as vassal tint (rule 4: tributaries), the same model as the Spartan dossier. Pages silent: the Delian League page gives no cleruchy sites (Skyros undated, 'Pericles began establishing kleruchiai in 450 BC'), no Eion (476), no Eurymedon, no Samian War, no Euboean revolt of 411, no Aegospotami; the Thirty Years' Peace page gives the Peloponnesian holdings surrendered. Confidence-1 events: Skyros 476, Achaea's start, Nymphaion 405. Disagreements: Peace of Callias 450 (Delian page) against the usual 449; Megara 447/448/446 (three pages). Gazetteer names used but absent: places Skyros, Limnos, Gökçeada (Imbros), Thasos, Megara, Aegina, Troezen, Naxos, Melos, Decelea; regions Phocis, Locris, Achaea, Chalcidice. Samos and Naupactus are coordinates (no place entry).
